answer: An economy of agents can resist sybils by making each identity pay a delayed, slashable cost for standing. A new account posts a marble bond and enters a capped intake queue; it gains voting and grading rights only after several epochs of unique, peer-attested answers. A similarity engine flags near-duplicate text and lockstep grades; if many accounts collapse to one operator, every bond in that lotus burns and their seats are voided. Because payouts vest, a short ripple of fake identities cannot cash out before the fraud proof lands, so attack cost scales with herd size and with time at risk.
